description: EXIT SECTION (ISO §2023:14.9.14 Format 4 / §2023:14.9.14.4 GR7) — a COBOL-2002 structured-procedure exit transferring control to the end of the current section (firing its PERFORM/SORT/USE return mechanism). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 Nucleus EXIT statement's general format is the bare word `EXIT` (§1985:VI.6.14.2), and §1985:VI.6.14.3 SR1 reads 'The EXIT statement must appear only in a sentence by itself and comprise the only sentence in the paragraph' (§1985:VI.6.14.4 GR1: 'An EXIT statement serves only to enable the user to assign a procedure-name to a given point in a program'); its one other EXIT is the Inter-Program Communication EXIT PROGRAM (§1985:X.5.4.1: 'The EXIT PROGRAM statement marks the logical end of a called program'). §2002:14.8.13 adds Format 5 `EXIT PERFORM [ CYCLE ]` and Format 6 `EXIT { PARAGRAPH | SECTION }`: 'The EXIT PERFORM statement provides a means of exiting an inline PERFORM (with or without returning to any specified test)' and 'The EXIT PARAGRAPH and EXIT SECTION statements provide a means of exiting a structured procedure without executing any of the following statements within the procedure', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 49: 'The ability to immediately exit an inline PERFORM statement, a paragraph, or a section has been added.' §2002:14.8.13.3 GR12: 'The execution of an EXIT SECTION statement causes control to be passed to an unnamed empty paragraph immediately following the last paragraph of the current section', and SR11 'The EXIT statement with the SECTION phrase may be specified only in a section'. §2014:14.9.13.3 GR12 prints the 2002 rule unchanged, so 2014 = 2023 (§2023:14.9.14.3 SR9 keeps SR11).
vcr: 2002 introduction (§2002:14.8.13 Format 6; §2002:F.2 item 49; no VCR row)
